title: feat(spec): the app item read answers by package id — 403 / 404 by the package key, per ADR-0048 §3.1
body:
Fixes #23183

Clause-②: yes

## What this does

ADR-0048 §3.1: "The route/container coordinate for an installed package's UI is its **package id** … With the current **one-app-per-package** invariant, the app *is* the package container." The console therefore opens an app at `/apps/PACKAGE_ID`. When that app is not in the caller's list, it must tell a withheld app (403) from a missing one (404). By name, the item read already answers that. By package id, no declared read did: `GET /api/v1/meta/app/com.acme.payroll` asked for an app NAMED `com.acme.payroll` and answered 404 whatever the package held.

The existing app item read now accepts a package id as its key, for `type: app` only, and answers the verdict the by-name read gives:

| caller / key | answer |
| :--- | :--- |
| a member on a withheld app's package id | `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, the by-name read's verdict (the message echoes the key the caller sent, never the app name) |
| a holder | `200`, the app under its own `name`, the same item the by-name read serves |
| an unknown package, a package with no app, a package whose app is unpublished (ADR-0045 §3), a package with more than one app | `404`, byte-identical to the answer for an unknown app name |
| a `packageId` / `?package=` naming a different package than the key | `400 INVALID_REQUEST` |
| a key in the package-id grammar on any other type | read by name, unchanged |

No separate verdict endpoint, no other type gains the arm, and the list read's withheld-drop is unchanged.

## Where it lands, and why it is not `rest-server.ts`

The card expected `GetMetaItemRequestSchema` plus `packages/rest`'s app item read. Measurement moved the runtime half to the producer, which the card's clause allows ("若实测表明真正的生产者在别包,直接按生产者侧修"):

- **Spec** (`packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`): `GetMetaItemRequestSchema.name` declares the arm. The new export `isAppPackageIdKey(type, name)` (`type === 'app'` and `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN`) is its one spelling. `GetMetaItemRequestSchema` is "still the protocol METHOD contract" (`plugin-rest-api.zod.ts`, the `GET /:type/:name` route entry), the input of `getMetaItem(request)` (`protocol.zod.ts`, the protocol interface).
- **Producer** (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, `resolveAppPackageIdKey`, called once at the top of `getMetaItem`): the key resolves to the package's one app, read by its own name scoped to that package. Two transports serve `GET /meta/:type/:name`: `RestServer`, and the runtime dispatcher behind `@objectstack/hono`'s catch-all. Both hand the protocol the key they were asked for and judge the envelope through the same `createMetaItemAnswer` chain (`meta-item-read-gate.ts`). The arm therefore reaches both with no transport code, and the per-caller gate judges the resolved app exactly as by name. A REST-only resolution would have left the catch-all host without the arm, and made the spec declaration false on the protocol face it declares.
- **REST** (`packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts`, `fetchCurrentMetaDocument`): `/history`, `/audit` and `/diff` judge "the item the plain read would judge" through `getMetaItem`, but read their own data under the literal `:name`. Without a guard they would judge the resolved app while serving the key's (empty) events. That gives a non-holder a 403 where history used to answer 200, and a holder a 200 empty diff where `/diff` used to answer the 404 absence. The guard asks `isAppPackageIdKey` and keeps those doors by name, as before. `meta-item-read-gate.ts` is untouched.

"The package's app" is what the package-scoped list serves (`getMetaItems({ type: 'app', packageId })`, the read behind `GET /meta/app?package=`). That covers the apps the package ships and its stored rows, and nothing for a disabled package. Drafts are in view exactly when the read reads drafts (`state: 'draft'` or `previewDrafts`).

### Readings the PM asked for

- **Zero apps:** 404 (the absence answer).
- **Two or more apps:** 404, plus one `console.warn` per package and app set naming the package and its apps with the remedy. One-app-per-package is enforced only by `defineStack` for `manifest.type === 'app'` (`validateSingleApp`, ADR-0019 D3). The shipped Setup/Studio/Account packages are `type: 'plugin'`, and the `/meta` save door does not enforce it either. A distinct "two apps" answer was rejected: it would let a caller see an app being built in the package (unpublished, ADR-0045 §3) before it is published.

## Premise verification (the ruling's falsifiable premise)

1. **Disjoint grammars: holds.** `AppSchema.name` is `SnakeCaseIdentifierSchema` (`/^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$/`, `ui/app.zod.ts`, `shared/identifiers.zod.ts`): no dot. `MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN` (`kernel/manifest.zod.ts`) requires at least one dot. Every mint path holds it: the `/meta` save door refuses a body whose `name` differs from the URL name (`savedItemNameRefusal`, 400) and then parses `AppSchema` (422), and `defineStack` parses `AppSchema`. A dotted app name is therefore never legal.
2. **No wider disclosure: holds.** Withheld gives 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`, the by-name verdict, and its message echoes the caller's own key, so the package-to-app-name mapping is not disclosed. Unpublished, service-gated, unknown, no-app and multi-app all give the same 404 bytes; the wire test pins unpublished against unknown on both hosts. The by-name control `/meta/app/payroll` answers the same 403 to the same member.

## For the objectui consumer (objectstack-ai/objectui#12285)

Probe the declared read `GET /api/v1/meta/app/PACKAGE_ID`, i.e. `client.meta.getItem('app', packageId)`, declared by `GetMetaItemRequestSchema.name` (recognise the key with `isAppPackageIdKey`). The existing `probeMetaItemAccess` mapping reads it unchanged: `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` maps to `denied`, the 404 with the absence code maps to `not_found`, and a `200` carrying `item` maps to `granted`. The `200` envelope's `name` is the app's own name.

## Tests

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.app-package-id-key.test.ts` (new, producer): covers one app (singular and plural type spelling), the by-name read, no app / unknown package, more than one app (absence plus one report), a `packageId` naming another package (`code` + `status`), the grammar on another type (discriminating: a package of that very id ships an app), and drafts.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-app-package-id-key.test.ts` (new, wire): `RestServer` and the hono catch-all, each over its own real store (better-sqlite3 `:memory:`, real `sys_metadata*`, real protocol). The triage pins run on both hosts: member 403 equals the by-name 403; holder 200 equals the by-name item; unknown package id 404 equals unknown app name bytes; unpublished package equals unknown package bytes; dotted key on `view` read by name. RestServer-only rows: `/history` and `/audit` stay by name for a builder who does not hold the app, and a holder's `/diff` stays the absence answer.

## Acceptance notes

- **Residue boundary.** The read doors stay open to pre-grammar residue rows by design (`METADATA_ITEM_NAME_PATTERN`'s note). A stored `app` row whose name is in the package-id grammar could only be residue, and the item read would now read that key as a package id. The row stays listable and deletable. Absent a named producer, not filed.
- **Disabled package.** The package-scoped list hides a disabled package's app, so the package-id key answers 404 for it. The by-name read does not consult the disabled flag. This is noted, not changed here.
- **Layered view.** `?layers=true` and `/layers` read through `getMetaItemLayered`, not `getMetaItem`, so they do not gain the arm, consistent with the ruling's "the existing app item read".
- **Two `rest-server.ts` comments routed to this dispatch** (seat 4's clock-out ledger). Both are outside this diff's touched region, so neither is changed here:
  - the `NormalizedRestServerConfig.api.documentation` comment names `documentation.enabled` and `responseFormat` as the `retiredKey()` tombstones but not `documentation.version`, which `rest-server.zod.ts` also tombstones, so it reads partially stale;
  - the `parseDeclaredApiConfig` paragraph was not re-measured beyond its location.
- **Declared file-surface deviation.** The claim's surface named `GetMetaItemRequestSchema` only in `protocol.zod.ts`, and `rest-server.ts` / `meta-item-read-gate.ts` for runtime. This diff also adds:
  - an import line and the `isAppPackageIdKey` export next to the schema, disjoint from #23428's describes;
  - the producer in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, under the card's clause;
  - a test in `@objectstack/runtime` that holds both hosts equal.
  In `rest-server.ts` it touches `fetchCurrentMetaDocument`, not the plain read handler.
